sum: An 18-day loop from Lukla across three passes above 5,300 m, taking in Chhukung, Everest Base Camp, Kala Patthar, the Gokyo lakes and the Thame valley.

guide.note: Khumbu has not enforced the national guide requirement, and experienced trekkers do walk this circuit independently. The passes are where a licensed guide matters most: the Kongma La and the Cho La cross moraine and glacier with no fixed trail, the line shifts every season, and in cloud or fresh snow people lose it within minutes. Do not cross any of the three alone.

access: Fly in and out of Lukla. Flights leave early from Kathmandu or, during the spring and autumn peaks, from Manthali in Ramechhap, and they stop as soon as cloud or wind builds. On a trek this long, lose a day to the weather at the start rather than hurry the acclimatization to make it up.

photo.a: Everest and Lhotse rise above dark rock ridges, with the grey Ngozumpa glacier and turquoise Gokyo lake in the valley below, seen from the Renjo La.
photo.c: Everest above Gokyo lake from the Renjo La

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
Sagarmatha park and Khumbu municipality permits
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
airport transfers; Kathmandu hotel nights in some packages

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park gate in Monjo, or in advance at the park counter in the Tourist Service Centre, Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality entry permit
permits.where: At the municipality's tourist information centre in Lukla when you land, or at the Monjo checkpoint if you walk in from the road. It cannot be bought in Kathmandu.

transportText: Flights to Lukla and back, from Kathmandu or (in the busy months) from Manthali with a night drive to the airstrip
tips: Build in two spare days. One usually goes on waiting for a pass to clear and the other on Lukla.
Carry microspikes and trekking poles for the Cho La. They weigh little and decide whether an icy morning is safe.
The evening before each pass, ask your lodge owner who came over that day and what the conditions were. It is the best forecast you will get.
Bring cash for the whole trek from Kathmandu or Namche. Prices rise with height, and the small lodges at Dzongla, Thagnak and Lungden take nothing else.
Keep water bottles inside your jacket on pass mornings; hoses and open bottles freeze within the first hour.

days.t: Fly to Lukla, walk to Phakding
days.note: Land at Lukla, meet your crew and walk down the valley to the river. The first day is short on purpose; tomorrow is the hill to Namche.
Permits are checked at Monjo. From the high bridge over the gorge it is a 600 m climb with no flat ground at all. Take two hours over it, not one.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Go up to the Everest View Hotel ridge and back, looping through Khumjung if your legs are good. The point is to climb high and sleep low; a day spent in the lodge does not do the same job.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: A level trail high above the river, then down to Phunki Tenga at 3,250 m and 600 m back up through forest to the monastery. The afternoon prayers are usually open to visitors.

Down through Deboche, across the Imja Khola and up to Pangboche, the last permanent village. Above it the trees end and the trail forks right into the Imja valley for Dingboche. Keep the evening quiet; you have gained 550 m.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 550 m, over the 500 m guideline, with no rest night before or after.

days.note: A gradual, stony trail up the Imja valley with the south wall of Lhotse filling the view ahead. Arrive for lunch and do very little afterwards: you are sleeping 320 m higher than last night.
why: About 1,300 m gained above 3,000 m without a rest night.

days.note: Climb the ridge north of the lodges: steep grass, then rock. Most people stop at the lower top near 5,400 m, which is enough for acclimatization. Be down by early afternoon, pack for the pass and ask who crossed today and what they found.

The longest day. Four to five hours of steady climbing past small lakes to the pass, a steep loose descent to the Khumbu Glacier and an hour across its rubble to Lobuche. There is no lodge and no dependable water in between. In bad weather walk round through Dingboche and Thukla.

days.t: Lobuche to Gorak Shep and Everest Base Camp
days.note: Follow the moraine to Gorak Shep by late morning, leave your pack and continue over glacier rubble to base camp and back. Agree a turnaround time before you set out and keep to it, wherever you have reached.

days.t: Kala Patthar, then down and across to Dzongla
days.note: Climb Kala Patthar in the cold before sunrise, eat at Gorak Shep and walk down past Lobuche. The Dzongla trail leaves the main valley before the drop to Thukla and contours above the lake of Chola Tsho. A long day, but you sleep 330 m lower.

Start at first light. A stream valley and then steep rock slabs lead to the edge of the glacier; follow the trodden line over the snow to the pass, three to four hours from Dzongla. The far side is a steep, loose descent, a climb over a spur and a long valley down to Thagnak.

days.t: Across the Ngozumpa Glacier to Gokyo
days.note: The path crosses the glacier over rubble and around melt ponds. Its line moves every season, so follow the newest cairns and other people's tracks, not an old map. You reach the lake with the afternoon free.

days.t: Gokyo Ri and a rest by the lake
days.note: Climb Gokyo Ri at dawn or for the evening light: 570 m and two to three hours up. Spend the remaining hours resting. This is the only slack day in the second half of the trek, and tomorrow is long.

Round the north shore of the lake, then a climb that steepens to the pass in three to four hours. Turn round often: Everest is behind you the whole way. A stone staircase leads down the west side past two lakes into a long, empty valley to Lungden.

Easy walking down the Bhote Koshi through Marlung and Taranga, on the old trade route from Tibet. Thame sits to one side of the valley below its monastery. Part of the village was destroyed by a flood in August 2024 and has been rebuilding since.
Cross the Bhote Koshi gorge on the bridge below Thame, then walk through Thamo and juniper woods to Namche. A half day, which leaves time for a hot shower and the first thick air in two weeks.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Steeply down to the river, along the valley and up the last rise into Lukla. Call at the airline office as soon as you arrive to reconfirm your seat for the morning.
Flights to Kathmandu or Manthali go from first light when the weather allows. If Lukla is closed you wait for the next clear morning, share a helicopter or start walking toward the road.
